faqs.a: Western (tropical) zodiac signs follow the Sun's apparent path through twelve 30° sectors of the sky, starting at the March equinox. Your sign is whichever sector the Sun was in on your birth date. It is an ancient calendar system, not a scientific measurement.

A cusp is a birth date on the boundary between two signs (for example, March 20–21). The exact changeover shifts slightly year to year. If you were born on a cusp, this tool shows the standard boundary — for precision you would need your birth time and an ephemeris.
No. There is no scientific evidence that birth dates influence personality. Astrology is entertainment and cultural tradition. Enjoy your sign, but make life decisions on evidence, not star signs.

The four classical elements group the signs: Fire (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius) is associated with energy; Earth (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn) with practicality; Air (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius) with intellect; Water (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces) with emotion. It is symbolism, not science.

This tool uses the Western tropical zodiac (Aries in March/April). Vedic (sidereal) astrology, common in India, uses slightly different date ranges shifted by about 24 days. If you follow Vedic astrology, your sign may differ.
faqs.q: Is this the same as Vedic astrology?

faqs.a: The dates drift by about a day over long periods because the tropical year is not a whole number of days. Most published tables — including this tool's — use the standard modern boundaries, which are fine for everyday use.
faqs.q: Do the date ranges ever change?

zodiac-sign-calculator.formula:

Sign boundaries (standard modern table):
Aries Mar 21–Apr 19 · Taurus Apr 20–May 20 · Gemini May 21–Jun 20
Cancer Jun 21–Jul 22 · Leo Jul 23–Aug 22 · Virgo Aug 23–Sep 22
Libra Sep 23–Oct 22 · Scorpio Oct 23–Nov 21 · Sagittarius Nov 22–Dec 21
Capricorn Dec 22–Jan 19 · Aquarius Jan 20–Feb 18 · Pisces Feb 19–Mar 20
